questiontext.text: A test path set satisfies Node Coverage but not Edge Coverage. What must be true?

answer.text: Every node is visited, but some edge is never traversed

feedback.text: Correct — edge coverage subsumes node coverage, not vice versa.
Then node coverage would already fail.
Prime path coverage would imply edge coverage.
With no branches, node coverage implies edge coverage.

generalfeedback.text: Edge coverage requires every edge; a branch can be skipped even when both its endpoints are visited via other paths.

questiontext.text: A prime path is a simple path that:

answer.text: Is not a proper subpath of any other simple path

feedback.text: Correct — maximal simple paths.

answer.text: Starts at the entry node and ends at the exit node

feedback.text: That describes a complete test path, not a prime path.
That is a Hamiltonian path.
A prime path may begin and end at the same node (a loop boundary).

generalfeedback.text: Prime paths are simple paths (no repeated nodes except possibly first = last) that are maximal — not proper subpaths of any other simple path.

questiontext.text: Which criterion subsumes Edge Coverage on a graph with at least one edge?

feedback.text: Correct — covering every path of length ≤ 2 covers every length-1 path.
Node coverage is weaker than edge coverage.
Statement coverage corresponds to node coverage.
Edge-pair, prime path and complete path all do.

generalfeedback.text: Edge-pair coverage requires all length-≤2 paths, which includes every single edge.

questiontext.text: In data-flow coverage, a DU pair for variable x is:

answer.text: A definition of x and a use of x reachable by a def-clear path

feedback.text: Correct.

answer.text: Any two statements that mention x

feedback.text: Mentions alone don't form a DU pair.
The second assignment kills the first definition.

answer.text: A use of x followed by its definition

feedback.text: Order is definition first, then use.

generalfeedback.text: A DU pair (d, u) needs a path from d to u with no intervening redefinition of x — a def-clear path.

questiontext.text: Complete Path Coverage is infeasible on any control-flow graph that contains a loop.

feedback.text: Correct — a loop yields infinitely many paths.
Loops create unbounded path counts, so complete path coverage cannot be finitely satisfied.

questiontext.text: stvisual reduces the selected test-path set with a greedy approximation of which classic problem? (two words)

feedback.text: Correct — greedy set cover.
Correct.

generalfeedback.text: Choosing a minimal set of test paths covering all requirements is the (NP-hard) set-cover problem; the tool uses the greedy approximation.
